summary: This Wikipedia-derived note covers Hamburg's governance and geography. It describes the Hamburg Rathaus as the seat of government since 1897 and traces mayors from Ole von Beust (2001-2010) through Christoph Ahlhaus and Olaf Scholz, including the black-green coalition and the later SPD-Greens coalition. It also describes Hamburg's location on the Elbe, its harbour and the Alster lakes, and the islands that belong to the city.
one_line: Overview of Hamburg's city government, mayoral history, coalitions, and its geographic setting on the Elbe and Alster lakes.
key_facts: Since 1897, the seat of the government of Hamburg has been the Hamburg Rathaus (Hamburg City Hall).
The Hamburg Rathaus houses the office of the mayor, the meeting room for the Senate and the floor for the Hamburg Parliament.
From 2001 until 2010, the mayor of Hamburg was Ole von Beust.
Ole von Beust governed in Germany's first statewide "black-green" coalition, consisting of the conservative CDU and the alternative GAL.
Christoph Ahlhaus briefly succeeded Ole von Beust as mayor in 2010.
The black-green coalition in Hamburg broke apart on November 28, 2010.
Olaf Scholz (SPD) became mayor of Hamburg on 7 March 2011.
After the 2015 election, the SPD and the Alliance 90/The Greens formed a coalition in Hamburg.
Hamburg is at a sheltered natural harbour on the southern fanning-out of the Jutland Peninsula.
Hamburg lies between Continental Europe to the south and Scandinavia to the north.
The North Sea lies to the west of Hamburg and the Baltic Sea lies to the northeast.
Hamburg is on the River Elbe at its confluence with the Alster and Bille.
The city centre is around the Binnenalster ("Inner Alster") and Außenalster ("Outer Alster").
The Binnenalster and Außenalster were both formed by damming the River Alster to create lakes.
The islands of Neuwerk, Scharhörn, and Nigehörn lie in the Hamburg Wadden Sea National Park and are part of the city of Hamburg.
